noticed_not_touched.what: The `drafting` guard in draft() reads the render-time state, so two calls within one React batch both see `false` and both call onDraft (a test that clicked twice inside one act() saw two calls). Between real separate clicks, the `disabled` attribute on the Draft button is what prevents a second call. A ref-based in-flight guard would make the guard itself effective.

assumptions: The fact row's second-step part is written '<k> second-step' and sits before 'limited' (e.g. '2 incoming · 2 outgoing · 1 second-step · limited'), following the finish line's example.
notes: Fix divergences from suggested_fix. F-007: followed the operator's upheld choice (add second-step to the fact row, keep the tab count). F-022: followed the suggestion (skip self-loops in groupRelationships), and also removed the second-step `to.id !== from.id` guard that this makes unreachable. That removal is why L3 reports invalid. F-019/F-020: tests added as suggested, plus a fixture per surviving mutant. P3 ('if (!onDraft || drafting)' -> 'if (!onDraft)') survives and cannot be killed by a DOM test. While a draft runs, the Draft button is rendered `disabled`, so a second user click dispatches no event and never reaches draft(). The only way to reach draft() twice without a re-render is two calls in one React batch, and there the guard reads the stale `false` and does not stop the second call either. In every DOM-reachable path the mutant behaves the same, so it is equivalent. The test 'Draft runs once while a session is opening…' pins the user-visible rule: the button reads 'Opening session…' and a second click makes no second call. An existing test was adapted, not weakened. 'relationship counts come from the root-adjacent edges and say when they are limited' asserted '2 incoming · 2 outgoing · limited' on a fixture that has a second-step edge, and under the upheld F-007 rule that text now carries '1 second-step'.
